structured_output.hypothesis: In North Sea plaice, weight at fixed length is lowest in the winter and early-spring quarter (Q1) and highest in the late-summer and autumn quarters. The amplitude of this cycle is markedly larger in mature (gonad-bearing) fish than in immature fish, and the trough coincides with the peak of spawning-stage maturity records.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Fit log10(individual weight) = a + b·log10(length) + quarter effect, separately for adult plaice (length ≥ 25 cm, maturity stage 2 or higher on the DATRAS maturity scale) and for juveniles (length < 20 cm or maturity stage 1). The claim passes only if all four conditions hold: (1) adult weight at standardised length (30 cm) in Q1 is at least 10% lower than in Q3, with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0; (2) the Q3/Q4 adult weight at fixed length exceeds Q1 by at least 10%, which gives the restoration; (3) the adult Q1-to-Q3 relative weight difference is at least 2 times the juvenile difference; (4) the quarter with the highest proportion of spawning-stage records (maturity code for 'spawning') is Q1, which is the quarter with the weight minimum.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if any of these holds: the adult Q1 weight at 30 cm is less than 5% below Q3, or its 95% CI includes 0; the adult cycle amplitude is less than 1.5 times the juvenile amplitude, which means a cycle not tied to maturity or spawning; or the spawning-stage peak falls in a different quarter from the weight minimum. Results between these thresholds are reported as inconclusive.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Weight of fish at unchanging length' is individual weight (IndWgt) conditional on length class (LngtClass), modelled as a length-weight regression with a seasonal term. Month is not available in all records, so the DATRAS Quarter field and the survey date are used. The months 'November to March/April' fall in Q4 and Q1, and 'May/June to November' fall in Q2 to Q4. 'Wholly caused by spawning and rebuilding' is operationalised as the cycle being much stronger in mature fish than in immature fish. A modern caveat is that DATRAS surveys are only Q1 and Q3 (IBTS), Q3 and Q4 (BTS and SNS), so the full November-to-June cycle can only be resolved coarsely by quarter. Feeding, temperature and sex confound the cycle, and 'wholly' cannot be proven. 'Spawning season can be determined from length and weight alone' is tested by whether the weight minimum identifies the same quarter as the independent maturity-stage data.

dataset.name: DATRAS (Database of Trawl Surveys): ICES data portal, biological sample (CA) records for North Sea IBTS, BTS and SNS surveys
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS provides freely downloadable raw exchange-format data and web services (icesDatras R package). The CA records for Pleuronectes platessa hold individual LngtClass, IndWgt, Sex, Maturity and Quarter/Year fields, which give weight at length, maturity stage and season across several surveys.
